text:
nina: RFC follow-up — proposing a thin adaptor layer between operator and control-plane for autoscaler decisions. TL;DR: split admit (policy/signals) from exec (actuation), return capacity hints + staleness metadata. Looking for tradeoffs and interface boundaries.

alex: quick q — how do we handle telemetry lag? control-plane decisions based on stale metrics could cause oscillation. fallback?

ryan: we hit this before. add explicit 'staleness_window' in the admit response. if metrics_age > window => control-plane responds with conservative admit. pseudocode: 
```
if metrics_age > window_ms:
  return { admit: "conservative", capacity_hint: null }
else:
  return decision
```

marta: rollout idea: make adaptor opt-in per-tenant behind feature-flag. canary to 5 tenants, run synthetic load, verify billing + latency. also need hooks so billing knows reserved vs burst capacity.

sam: policy surface question — should /admit be a declarative DSL (JSON) or opaque webhook returning tokens? I lean DSL with priority bands so operator can implement fairness locally and simulate decisions.

infra-bot: deploybot: canary deployed autoscale-adaptor v0.2 to staging :rocket:

alex: another edge: mixed-gpu clusters + preemptible capacity. admit needs to include type-aware hints (gpu_types, quantization_profile) and an eviction_penalty estimate so control-plane avoids short-lived reservations.

nina: agreed. plan: extend /admit response shape to include: 
```
{
  admit: "allow|deny|conservative",
  reason: "string",
  metrics_age_ms: int,
  capacity_hint: "gpuA100,gpuH100",
  eviction_risk: "0.0-1.0",
  suggested_ttl_sec: int
}
```
will iterate on names.

ryan: add intent_id uuid in admit so traces correlate. observability: histograms for admit_latency_ms and decision_delta_tokens.

marta: +1 runbook item: operator unreachable -> fallback to local conservative policy + emit alert to #eng-oncall. include playbook steps. :thumbsup:

sam: I'll draft a few DSL examples this afternoon. example quick sketch: `{ priority: "latency", weight: 0.7, min_tokens: 10, burst_tokens: 5 }` — want to validate semantics with runtime.

nina: next steps: PR with proto + unit tests by EOD Wed. reviewers @alex @sam. I'll also post a concise design doc: https://redwood.internal/rfcs/autoscale-adaptor (work-in-progress).

alex: nits — be explicit about the allowed failure modes (control-plane slow, operator crash, partial connectivity). prefer conservative admit semantics that bias towards availability.

nina: noted. I'll add a failure-mode matrix in the doc. thanks everyone — let's keep discussion in this thread and I'll update the RFC with the proto patch.
